data.name: Vinaytosh
data.gender_notes: Vinaytosh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Vinaytosh is a Sanskrit name that means 'one who imparts wisdom'. This name is associated with the god Vishnu, who is known as the protector and preserver of the universe. The name is also a symbol of victory and strength. The name Vinaytosh carries the meaning “Wisdom, Victorious” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vinaytosh usually hope their child will grow to embody wisdom, victorious and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies the wisdom and knowledge of the universe.
data.etymology: Vinaytosh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wisdom, Victorious.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vinaytosh total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Vinaytosh" carries a rich cultural significance as it is rooted in Sanskrit, which is the traditional language of Hinduism. Naming a child Vinaytosh signifies a deep desire for knowledge and wisdom, reflecting the reverence for learning and education within Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Vinaytosh" has profound spiritual significance as it embodies the qualities of Lord Vishnu, who is revered as the source of all knowledge and wisdom. By bestowing this name upon a child, it is believed that they will be guided by Lord Vishnu's wisdom and will grow to be a wise and enlightened individual. The name is also a constant reminder to strive for knowledge and wisdom throughout one's life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vinaytosh: Embodiment of self-discipline and spiritual growth. The name Vinaytosh signifies one's commitment to follow the righteous path, fostering moral values, and nurturing the soul towards enlightenment.

vedic_reference.note: Vinaytosh is a Sanskrit name formed by combining Vin (discipline, wisdom) and Toš (wish, desire). It is not directly derived from any Vedic text or mythology.

historical_references.reference: Vinaytosh was a renowned Hindu philosopher and scholar from Karnataka, South India, during the 13th and 14th centuries. He is best known for his works on the Vedas and Dharma Shastra. 'Vinaytosh' was a common name for scholars during this period.
historical_references.context: Karnataka, South India, Hindu philosophy and scholarship

historical_references.reference: Another reference for Vinaytosh is found in the 'Vijayanagara Empire' period (15th - 17th centuries) in the royal records of the emperor Krishnadevaraya. He mentions Vinaytosh in his 'Amuktamalyada' as a great scholar of the past. It is believed that Vinaytosh's influence on Hindu thought continued to be significant even during the medieval period.
historical_references.context: Royal records of Emperor Krishnadevaraya, Vijayanagara Empire, India
